about: Reading the new, complete lines of a log file another process is still writing. Nothing past the last newline is consumed until it has a newline after it, so an error marker cut by a poll boundary is never missed. A file that shrank is read again from the start; a missing file yields nothing. Each case is a list of steps on one file: 'append' adds text, 'set' replaces the whole content, 'remove' deletes the file, 'poll' reads and reports the lines returned and the offset afterwards. Empty lines with a bare newline are dropped; a line that is only a carriage return comes back as an empty string (the C# behaviour).

cases.name: a line still being written is held back until it is finished
the offset does not move over an unfinished line
a shrunk file is read from the start again
a missing file yields nothing rather than failing
every line of a many-line batch comes back
